title: Kundalini climbs to meet Shiva
hookLine: the sleeper wakes and climbs, lotus by lotus, to a meeting at the crown
carry: at the crown, shakti and shiva are one
tomorrow: why would a map of the body have letters on its petals?

lines: SHE RISES, ONE LOTUS AT A TIME.
cards: An elevator in a tall building chimes at every floor, and every time the doors slide open on a different hallway. The old map has a journey like that, only slower.
The serpent who slept across the door at the base of the spine has lifted her head. The road is open.
And she begins to rise, one lotus at a time, each one turning toward her as she passes, toward a place at the very top that she has never reached.

teach.b: The Sat-Cakra-Nirupana tells the climb center by center. She passes the root, the lotuses above it, the heart with its unstruck sound, the throat, the place between the brows.
Each station has its own shape and sound, and the meditator follows her with attention, stop by stop.
Then, above them all, at the crown, the text sets a lotus of a thousand petals: Sahasrara. That's where she's going. And when she arrives, she isn't alone.
There, the text says, kundalini, Shakti, the Goddess as power, unites with Shiva. So the top of the map isn't a light switching on.
And under the meeting sits one of tantra's biggest teachings: Shakti and Shiva are never truly two. Shiva is pure awareness; Shakti is the power that moves, and everything that moves is her.

The climb is that power coming home to its own source. It's why Hindu homes and temples so often show Shiva and Parvati side by side, and sometimes as one figure, Ardhanarishvara, half him and half her.
The Sri Yantra's point held the same two as one. A thousand petals inside the skull?
The text isn't asking that. Some readers take the thousand as fullness, more than anyone could count. And the story isn't finished at the summit.
The text has one more page, and it comes later in the run.

how: In kundalini meditation as the tantric texts describe it, practitioners move attention upward center by center toward the crown, usually under a teacher's guidance.

games.q: what does “the chakras as a map” mean?
o: a race to switch on a light inside the head
a climb, lotus by lotus, to a meeting at the top
a ladder of moods from sad up to happy

p: the thousand-petaled lotus at the crown
the one she meets at the top
lotus by lotus, stop by stop

s: the top of the map is a light that switches on
the text pictures a meeting: Shakti uniting with Shiva.
the crown lotus is given a thousand petals
the Sat-Cakra-Nirupana says so; some readers take the thousand as fullness.
in the text, kundalini jumps straight from the base to the crown
she rises lotus by lotus, every station on the way.

games.q: at the temple, a friend sees a statue that's half Shiva, half Parvati, in one body. she asks why. what fits today's teaching?
o: in tantra Shakti and Shiva are never truly two: power and awareness, one reality.
it shows the two gods had a fight and were stitched back together.
it's only an art style; there's no meaning behind it.
games.why: Ardhanarishvara, the lord who is half woman, shows what the chakra map climbs toward: Shakti meeting Shiva, the two held as one.

practice: Close your eyes and rest your attention at the base of your spine. With each slow breath, let it climb a little: the belly, the heart, the throat, the brow, the crown.
At the top, don't reach for anything; stay there, and let it be a meeting rather than a finish line.

wordCard.voice: The chakras as a map: a climb, lotus by lotus, to Sahasrara, the thousand-petaled crown, where Shakti and Shiva meet.

orig.note: Sanskrit: thousand-spoked; the lotus at the crown of the head.

carryVoice: Your line: at the crown, Shakti and Shiva are one. The power comes home to its source. Day sixteen forty-six, climbed.

sources.ref: Sat-Cakra-Nirupana (kundalini rising through the centers; the thousand-petaled lotus at the crown; her union with Shiva there)
Ardhanarishvara in Hindu temple art (Shiva and Parvati shown as one figure, half male and half female)
